system.name: CROSSAGENTIE
system.one_liner: A multi-agent LLM framework for zero-shot information extraction: type agents debate conflicting NER and RE labels, then a single LLM is fine-tuned on the outputs.

content.variant_note: three zoom columns: the main process on the left, three stacked dashed collaboration stages in the middle, and one detail panel per stage on the right joined by magnifier arrows, with an inference row along the bottom
content.argues: Agents per entity or relation type resolve conflicting labels through grouped and cross-task discussion, and the resolved outputs can be distilled into one LLM for cheap inference.
content.subject: the four-stage CROSSAGENTIE process followed on one sentence about Reagon and America, with agent dialogue and conflict tables

lessons.what_to_learn: Zoom a multi-stage method in three columns: the whole process, its stage boxes, then one detail panel per stage; give each stage one colour that returns on its panel, join them with magnifier arrows and run one tiny example through the details.
lessons.suits: multi-stage or multi-agent LLM frameworks whose stages need a worked example, such as debate, verification or refinement loops over structured outputs.

evidence: illustrates the multi-agent collaboration process through four stages, converting an input document into structured outputs
NER agents initially misclassify “America” as both ORG and LOC.

summary: CrossAgentIE is a multi-agent framework for zero-shot information extraction in which LLM agents for each entity and relation type debate conflicting labels, after which a single LLM is fine-tuned on their outputs. Figure 1 is organised in three zoom levels. The left column shows the main process: an input sentence goes through a Multi-Agents Collaboration box to an output table, then Template Fine-Tuning trains a single LLM that handles inference. The middle column opens the collaboration into three dashed stages (type-agent setup in yellow, intra-group cross-type discussion in green, inter-group cross-task discussion in pink). The right column gives each stage a detail panel, joined by magnifier arrows, that follows the example Reagon and America from conflicting labels to a resolved result.
summary_zh: CrossAgentIE 让各类型的 LLM 智能体辩论冲突标签，再把结果蒸馏到单个模型。图一按三级放大排布：左列主流程，中列三个彩色虚线阶段，右列用放大镜箭头连到各阶段细节，并用 Reagon / America 例子走完冲突与消解。
notes: Prior kinds kept (stage-pipeline, actor-interaction) and worked-walkthrough added because the right column follows one sentence through the stages; variant is my own slug because the columns are zoom levels rather than a plain chain. Robot icon count of 26 is an approximate count of placements read from the picture. The roles of the two robot columns and the central robot in Bidirectional Refinement are read from the text 'NER feedback to RE and RE feedback to NER'; the figure itself does not say what the central robot is. The spelling Reagon appears in tables and Reagan in the sentence.
